question: Should OpenClaw accept this PR's default-on `memory.isolation` config/API direction as the memory-core path for multi-user partitioning?
rationale: The patch defines a new security-sensitive memory partition contract, new config defaults, and QMD/builtin storage behavior; automation can identify blockers, but maintainers must decide whether this is the desired product/API shape.

options.title: Sponsor guarded rework
options.body: Keep the direction alive only as a rebased patch that fixes default/config semantics and includes redacted two-user builtin/QMD proof.

options.title: Hold under canonical issue
options.body: Pause this branch and use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/63550 for the product and security design before accepting a config surface.

options.title: Decline core surface
options.body: Close this PR if maintainers decide per-user memory isolation should stay in deployment guidance or an external/plugin design rather than memory-core config.

recommendation.title: Sponsor guarded rework
recommendation.body: Keep the direction alive only as a rebased patch that fixes default/config semantics and includes redacted two-user builtin/QMD proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows broad memory, config, filesystem-safety, and security-boundary work across the affected surfaces.
